headline.headline: WINNER TAKE ALL: SABRES AND CANADIENS MEET IN GAME 7 FOR A SHOT AT THE HURRICANES
headline.deck: Buffalo and Montreal settle a bitter Atlantic Division rivalry with a trip to the Eastern Conference finals on the line.
headline.body:
BUFFALO, N.Y. -- Fifty games of regular-season separation and two rounds of playoff warfare have come down to this: the Buffalo Sabres and the Montreal Canadiens will skate onto the ice Monday night for a winner-take-all Game 7, with a berth in the Eastern Conference finals waiting for whoever survives. The Carolina Hurricanes, having already punched their ticket to the next round, will be watching from Raleigh.

The Sabres, who finished the regular season at 50-23-9, carry the better record and home-ice advantage into Game 7, but Montreal refused to be buried. The Canadiens, 48-24-10 on the year, have clawed back from multiple must-win moments throughout this series, leaning on goaltending and disciplined defensive structure to keep Buffalo's high-powered offense from running away with it. Neither club has shown any willingness to blink.

Buffalo will need its top forwards to break through against a Montreal blue line that has tightened considerably as the series has worn on. The Canadiens, for their part, understand that a road victory in a Game 7 would represent one of the more stunning upsets of this playoff year. Puck drop is Monday evening, and all of the pressure, all of the regular-season swagger, means nothing now. One game, one winner, one spot in the final four.

secondary.headline: CAVALIERS STEAMROLL INTO EASTERN FINALS, SET SIGHTS ON KNICKS
secondary.deck: Cleveland's 31-point demolition of Detroit sets up a marquee Eastern Conference finals showdown.
secondary.body:
CLEVELAND -- The Detroit Pistons arrived in Cleveland hoping to extend their improbable playoff run. They left Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse on the wrong end of a 125-94 drubbing, as the Cleveland Cavaliers closed out their second-round series with clinical efficiency and advanced to face the New York Knicks in the Eastern Conference finals.

Cleveland controlled the game from the opening tip, building a lead that Detroit could never chip away at. The Cavaliers' defense smothered the Pistons' halfcourt offense while Cleveland's transition game ran Detroit ragged in the second half. The Knicks, who are waiting on the other side of the bracket, will present a far sterner test, and the chess match between those two franchises figures to be one of the most closely watched series of the spring.

secondary.headline: PHILLIES BLANK PIRATES, 6-0, AS PHILADELPHIA ROTATION ROLLS
secondary.deck: Philadelphia's pitching staff delivers a complete shutout to keep the Phillies surging in May.
secondary.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The Pittsburgh Pirates came to Citizens Bank Park and left with nothing. The Philadelphia Phillies posted a 6-0 shutout on Sunday, a dominant performance that underscored just how dangerous Philadelphia's pitching staff has become heading into the heart of the 2026 season. The Phillies' offense provided more than enough cushion, but it was the arms that told the real story.

The result adds further irony to an early-season narrative that has surprised many analysts. Pittsburgh entered 2026 as one of baseball's more talked-about surprise clubs, but Sunday's performance reminded the league that the Phillies have no intention of letting any team build momentum at their expense. Philadelphia has now positioned itself firmly among the National League's most complete clubs as the calendar turns toward the summer stretch.

secondary.headline: NASHVILLE EXPECTED TO LAND SUPER BOWL LXIV IN 2030 AS NFL OWNERS CONVENE
secondary.deck: League owners gather Tuesday and are poised to award Music City its first Super Bowl.
secondary.body:
NEW YORK -- The NFL is expected to make it official on Tuesday: Nashville will host Super Bowl LXIV in 2030, when league owners gather for their spring meetings and cast what sources describe as a nearly certain vote in the Tennessee capital's favor. The announcement would mark a significant milestone for a franchise city that has invested heavily in its sporting infrastructure.

Nashville's bid has gained momentum over the past several months as the city's new stadium project has impressed league officials. The vote would give the Tennessee Titans a showcase moment on the grandest stage in American sports, and it would extend the NFL's recent pattern of bringing the Super Bowl to newer markets. Owners are also expected to address several other agenda items during the spring meetings, including ongoing negotiations around the league's international scheduling package.

column.headline: GAME 7 IS WHAT SPORTS IS SUPPOSED TO FEEL LIKE
column.body:
There is no better unit of measurement in team sports than a Game 7. No best-of-seven series ever devised a more honest conclusion. Buffalo and Montreal have skated through two rounds, weathered injuries, bad bounces, and crowd noise, and now they must distill everything into one regulation's worth of hockey on Monday night. The Cavaliers got their decisive game and blew the doors off Detroit. The Sabres and Canadiens have earned something rawer and more uncertain than that.

The Hurricanes are sitting in Raleigh doing film work on two possible opponents, and that waiting is its own kind of luxury. Whoever emerges from Game 7 will be battle-hardened in a way Carolina simply cannot replicate by watching tape. Buffalo has the record, the home ice, and the crowd. Montreal has the nerve. That is a genuinely compelling argument, and the sport deserves every second of the debate. Monday night cannot come soon enough.

story.headline: BRAVES BLUDGEON RED SOX, 8-1, AS ATLANTA OFFENSE ERUPTS IN BOSTON
story.deck: Atlanta pounds Boston pitching for eight runs, handing Red Sox their worst home loss of the season.
story.body:
BOSTON — The Atlanta Braves turned Fenway Park into a house of horrors Sunday, pummeling the Red Sox 8-1 in a one-sided affair that left the home crowd filing toward the exits well before the final out. Atlanta's lineup carved through Boston's pitching rotation with relentless efficiency, sending runners around the bases in bunches and silencing a Fenway crowd that had little to cheer about from the opening inning onward.

The Braves wasted no time establishing their dominance, building an early multi-run cushion that Boston's bats never came close to erasing. Atlanta's starter kept the Red Sox offense in check throughout, allowing just one run while the Braves continued to pile on. The eight-run output was a statement performance from a club that has quietly positioned itself as one of the National League's most dangerous teams heading into the summer stretch.

Elsewhere around the majors Sunday, the Cleveland Guardians rolled past the Cincinnati Reds 10-3 in an Ohio showdown, and the Philadelphia Phillies blanked the Pittsburgh Pirates 6-0 behind a dominant pitching performance. The Tampa Bay Rays edged the Miami Marlins 6-3 to stay hot, while the Baltimore Orioles topped the Washington Nationals 7-3 and the Toronto Blue Jays defeated the Detroit Tigers 4-1.

story.headline: CAVALIERS CRUSH PISTONS IN GAME 7, ADVANCE TO FACE KNICKS IN EASTERN FINALS
story.deck: Cleveland dominates Detroit 125-94 to punch ticket to Conference Finals
story.body:
DETROIT -- The Cleveland Cavaliers left no doubt and no drama at Little Caesars Arena on Sunday night, dismantling the Detroit Pistons 125-94 in a brutal Game 7 to advance to the Eastern Conference Finals. The 31-point margin was a statement as much as a victory, Cleveland's starters pouring it on from the opening tip and never allowing Detroit so much as a foothold in a winner-take-all game that turned into anything but a contest.

The Pistons, who had clawed and scrapped their way to a seventh game against one of the East's elite, simply ran out of answers against Cleveland's suffocating defense and a Cavaliers offense that found its rhythm early and never lost it. Detroit's young core, which had shown flashes of genuine promise throughout the series, was overwhelmed by the moment and by a Cleveland squad that has championship ambitions written across every rotation.

The loss ends a Pistons season that carried genuine excitement into the postseason but ultimately exposed the gap between a franchise still rebuilding and one already built to win. The Cavaliers now head to New York, where they will open the Eastern Conference Finals against Jalen Brunson and the Knicks, a series that figures to be a far more punishing and closely contested affair than what Cleveland dispatched Sunday night in Detroit.

story.headline: SABRES AND CANADIENS COLLIDE IN WINNER-TAKE-ALL GAME 7 WITH CAROLINA WAITING
story.deck: Buffalo and Montreal settle their second-round series tonight, with the Hurricanes watching from afar.
story.body:
BUFFALO, N.Y. — The puck drops tonight at KeyBank Center and only one team skates out alive. The Buffalo Sabres, who finished the regular season with 50 wins and the best record in the Atlantic Division, host the Montreal Canadiens in a Game 7 that will determine which franchise faces the Carolina Hurricanes in the Eastern Conference finals. Buffalo forward Tage Thompson, who has posted six goals and four assists this series, carries the heaviest offensive burden for the home side, while Canadiens center Nick Suzuki has been equally relentless, tallying five goals and six assists to keep Montreal alive through six bruising games.

The keys for Buffalo, according to analyst Greg Wyshynski, run directly through goaltender Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen. The Finnish netminder allowed three goals in Game 6 on 28 shots, a performance the Sabres cannot afford to repeat on home ice. Coach Lindy Ruff has stressed puck possession in the neutral zone and limiting Montreal's transition game, where winger Juraj Slafkovsky has burned Buffalo twice with odd-man rushes. The Canadiens, who went 48-24-10 this season, have demonstrated they will not fold under pressure, having won two elimination games already in this series.

In Las Vegas, oddsmakers have installed the Carolina Hurricanes as the heavy favorites to represent the East in the Stanley Cup Final, with Colorado and Vegas remaining the top picks league-wide for the championship. The Hurricanes, rested and disciplined under Rod Brind'Amour, have had days to prepare for whichever battered opponent emerges tonight. Puck drop is scheduled for 7 p.m. Eastern, and the winner gets precious little time to recover before Carolina's buzzsaw arrives.

story.headline: DRAFT GRADES ARE IN: ANALYSTS SPLIT ON WHO WON AND LOST THE 2026 NFL DRAFT
story.deck: Some franchises earned high marks while others left experts scratching their heads.
story.body:
Three weeks removed from the 2026 NFL Draft in Green Bay, the grades are rolling in and the verdicts are anything but unanimous. The Cleveland Browns drew widespread praise for selecting Tennessee quarterback Malik Sorrells at No. 4 overall, giving the long-suffering franchise its most celebrated prospect since Baker Mayfield. Meanwhile, the Las Vegas Raiders parlayed a flurry of trades down the board into five picks in the first three rounds, stockpiling youth at a cost that left some talent evaluators uneasy about the team's win-now ambitions.

The New England Patriots, picking eighth overall for the second straight year, drew mixed reviews after tabbing Georgia linebacker Darius Cobb rather than addressing a wide receiver corps that ranked dead last in yards per game during the 2025 season. Head coach Jerod Mayo defended the selection at the team's post-draft press conference, pointing to Cobb's rare combination of speed and football IQ as the driving factor. Several analysts pushed back, noting that veteran free agent receiver Tyrese Holloway remains unsigned and available at a reasonable price.

On the free agency front, the Dallas Cowboys made headlines Monday by agreeing to terms with former Pittsburgh Steelers left tackle Germaine Okafor on a three-year deal worth a reported $54 million, shoring up a blindside that cost three different quarterbacks playing time last season due to injury. The San Francisco 49ers, still rebuilding after a 7-10 finish in 2025, quietly added depth at cornerback by signing Marcus Teel away from the Carolina Panthers. Training camps are still two months away, but the early movers have already separated themselves from the pack.
